description: Weight of the radar's ACC target speed in fused's per-track speed filter: 2.4 (sigma 0.5 m/s), 2.5 (0.3 m/s) and the ACC target's values copied unblended for its track. Unchanged openpilot card -> radard -> planner replays: the 27 replay drives (gate counts as in docs/09) and the hindsight-lead oracle (oracle_reference.json), plus the road drives (owner 2.1 drives and a second car, open loop). Gates were fixed before the 0.3 result.

acc_values_unblended.note: the extra further-drive hard tick is a moment where the radar's own ACC tracker slides off a real car at about 85 m (closing -10.6 m/s, 2.9 m sideways on a straight road) while the camera keeps the lead at ego speed: unblended -2.1 m/s2 (published lead -11.1 m/s), 2.4 -1.2 (-8.1), 2.5 -1.0 (-7.5): the blend keeps the published speed between the two radar estimates (2.5 keeps 2.4's further count)

2.5.owner_mild_note: the added mild request is judged real (driver or camera confirms the slowdown)

caveat: The oracle's reference takes its range from the ACC target where present, so it partly favours a heavier ACC weight; the hard-tick, onset and anticipation counts are independent of it and are equal or slightly better; held-out target episodes rose 3 -> 4 and road mild requests 7 -> 8 (judged real).
basis: sigma 0.3 m/s is closer than 0.5 to a likelihood fit of the ACC target's noise near range (about 0.13 m/s; the fit is degenerate because errors persist, so it bounds rather than sets the value); earlier tests of a heavier ACC weight used the ACC speed at 0.1 m/s per code, 20 % too small (acc_summary_units.json).
